title: Distinctness conjecture for the values of the divisor-sum ratio
statement:
Let $\sigma(x)$ denote the sum-of-divisors function for $x\in\mathbb{N}$. **Distinctness conjecture.** All values of

$$
\frac{\sigma(x)}{x^2}
$$

for $x\in\mathbb{N}$ are pairwise distinct. No equal values are known for different natural numbers, although distinctness is known for different coprime numbers. The conjecture concerns whether the function $x\mapsto \sigma(x)/x^2$ is injective on $\mathbb{N}$.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.15628

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2023).
source_name: Mario Ziller, “Orders and partitions of integers induced by arithmetic functions”, arXiv:2310.15628 (2026).
